17.​Amend paragraph 44 (Swansea) 
 
The Starmer government is one of crisis. It came to power with a massive parliamentary 
majority, but in reality it had only received the lowest vote share of any party forming a 
majority government in post-war British history. After 14 years of Tory attacks there was a 
yearning for change. But there has been no change. In fact, things are deteriorating. There is 
a widespread feeling of betrayal and disgust. At the time of writing, Starmer’s personal 
favourability rating is at minus 51 percent, while Reeves’ standing is at minus 57 percent. 
She is the most unpopular chancellor since records began. Starmer is widely regarded as 
out of touch with ordinary people: more comfortable abroad or hosting meetings of his 
‘coalition of the willing’, rather than dealing with domestic problems.  the representative of a 
feeble political establishment both unable and unwilling to enact real change, whose 
domestic policies have failed to adequately address declining living standards. As a 
result, Labour languishes at less than 20 percent in the opinion polls, and has been pushed 
behind the Greens according to some surveys. 
 
CC recommendation: Accept 
 
18.​Add after paragraph 61 and renumber (Reading 1) 
 
Out of all the advanced capitalist nations the British military stands as one of the 
weakest, the actual deployable personnel of the British army could be as low as 
54,000 equal to two months of Russian casualties in Ukraine. The uk has 180,000 
troops total, to put that in comparison the United States marine corps has a similarly 
sized force, while having more aircraft than the British army has in its whole force.  
Because of this the UK is reliant on the far larger American army in its defensive and 
foreign policy. The uk cannot act as an independent military force on the world stage 
and because of this they need to lean on another global power or defensive block 
however the only viable power for the uk remains the US. 
 
CC recommendation: Reject in favour of amendment 21 
 
19.​Add after paragraph 61 and renumber (Reading 2) 
 
The growing contradiction between the interests of the American bourgeoisie and 
British bourgeoisie increasingly puts pressure on the UK to solve its military 
weakness. However, they have no money, and no one wants to join the army. To gain 
funding they would need to cut spending. To get troops they would need to reinstitute 
national service, a policy already attempted by the previous conservative government. 
Yet either of these decisions would have the potential to significantly radicalise the 
British youth who would face the brunt of this attack. 
CC recommendation: Reject in favour of amendment 21
